title: Diffusion Models & Stable Diffusion
description: Diffusion Models: State-of-the-art image generation! Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 2, Midjourney'in arkasındaki teknoloji. Process: (1) Forward Diffusion: Clean image → Gradually add noise → Pure noise. (2) Reverse Diffusion: Pure noise → Gradually denoise → Clean image! Learn reverse process with neural network. Math: Markov chain, Gaussian noise, score matching. Architecture: U-Net + attention, timestep embedding, conditioning (text→image via CLIP). Training: Denoise images at different noise levels. Sampling: Start from random noise, iteratively denoise (50-1000 steps). Advantages vs GANs: Training stability, mode coverage, controllability. Applications: Text-to-image (Stable Diffusion), inpainting, super-resolution, image editing. Latent diffusion: Work in compressed latent space (faster!). Real-world: Stable Diffusion XL, DALL-E 2, Imagen, Midjourney.

content.level0_basic: Diffusion Models: Reverse engineering of noise! Analogy: Video backwards: Clear image → blur → static noise. Then learn to reverse: Static → gradually sharper → clear image! Process: (1) Training: Take image, add noise gradually (1000 steps). Learn to predict: 'What was previous less-noisy version?' (2) Generation: Start random noise, repeatedly ask 'less noisy version?' → Final: Real-looking image! Text-to-image: Add text guidance. 'Cat wearing sunglasses' → conditions denoising process → generates that image! Why better than GANs? (1) Training more stable. (2) Higher quality. (3) Better diversity. (4) Controllability via guidance. Models: Stable Diffusion (open-source), DALL-E 2 (OpenAI), Midjourney (commercial). Speed: ~5-50 seconds per image (vs GAN's instant). Quality: Photorealistic! Revolutionary for AI art!
content.level1_beginner:
**Diffusion Process:**

```
Forward (Destroy):
  x₀ (clean) → x₁ → x₂ → ... → xₜ (noise)
  Gradually add Gaussian noise
  
Reverse (Generate):
  xₜ (noise) → ... → x₂ → x₁ → x₀ (clean)
  Trained neural net removes noise
```

**Training:**

```python
# 1. Take clean image x₀
# 2. Sample timestep t (1 to 1000)
# 3. Add noise: xₜ = √(αₜ)·x₀ + √(1-αₜ)·ε
#    where ε ~ N(0,I) is noise
# 4. Train model to predict ε from xₜ and t
# 5. Loss: ||ε - ε_predicted||²
```

**Generation:**

```python
# Start: x₁₀₀₀ ~ N(0,I)  # Random noise
# Iterate: t = 1000 → 0
for t in reversed(range(1000)):
    # Predict noise
    ε = model(xₜ, t)
    # Denoise one step
    xₜ₋₁ = denoise(xₜ, ε, t)
# Result: x₀ is generated image!
```

**Stable Diffusion Architecture:**

```
Input: Noisy image xₜ + timestep t + text prompt

1. Text → CLIP embedding
2. xₜ → VAE encoder → Latent zₜ
3. U-Net(zₜ, t, text_embedding) → Predicted noise
4. Denoise: zₜ₋₁ = zₜ - noise
5. After 50 steps: z₀ → VAE decoder → Image!

Key: Work in latent space (512×512 → 64×64 latent)
     Much faster! 'Latent Diffusion'
```

**Text Conditioning (Classifier-Free Guidance):**

```
Unconditional: ε = model(xₜ, t, empty)
Conditional: ε_cond = model(xₜ, t, "cat")

Guided: ε = ε + scale·(ε_cond - ε)
Scale (CFG): 7-15 typical
  Low → diverse but less accurate
  High → accurate but less creative
```
content.level2_application:
**Simplified Diffusion Implementation:**

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class SimpleDiffusion:
    def __init__(self, timesteps=1000):
        self.timesteps = timesteps
        # Variance schedule (linear)
        self.betas = torch.linspace(1e-4, 0.02, timesteps)
        self.alphas = 1 - self.betas
        self.alphas_cumprod = torch.cumprod(self.alphas, 0)
    
    def forward_diffusion(self, x0, t):
        """Add noise to x0 at timestep t"""
        noise = torch.randn_like(x0)
        sqrt_alpha = torch.sqrt(self.alphas_cumprod[t])
        sqrt_one_minus_alpha = torch.sqrt(1 - self.alphas_cumprod[t])
        
        # xt = √(ᾱₜ)·x₀ + √(1-ᾱₜ)·ε
        xt = sqrt_alpha * x0 + sqrt_one_minus_alpha * noise
        return xt, noise
    
    def train_step(self, model, x0):
        """One training step"""
        # Random timestep
        t = torch.randint(0, self.timesteps, (x0.shape[0],))
        
        # Add noise
        xt, noise = self.forward_diffusion(x0, t)
        
        # Predict noise
        predicted_noise = model(xt, t)
        
        # Loss
        loss = nn.MSELoss()(noise, predicted_noise)
        return loss
    
    @torch.no_grad()
    def sample(self, model, shape):
        """Generate images"""
        # Start from noise
        x = torch.randn(shape)
        
        # Iteratively denoise
        for t in reversed(range(self.timesteps)):
            # Predict noise
            t_tensor = torch.full((shape[0],), t)
            predicted_noise = model(x, t_tensor)
            
            # Denoise
            alpha = self.alphas[t]
            alpha_cumprod = self.alphas_cumprod[t]
            beta = self.betas[t]
            
            # DDPM sampling formula
            if t > 0:
                noise = torch.randn_like(x)
            else:
                noise = 0
            
            x = (1 / torch.sqrt(alpha)) * (
                x - ((1 - alpha) / torch.sqrt(1 - alpha_cumprod)) * predicted_noise
            ) + torch.sqrt(beta) * noise
        
        return x

# Usage
diffusion = SimpleDiffusion(timesteps=1000)
generated_images = diffusion.sample(model, shape=(4, 3, 64, 64))
```
content.level3_advanced:
**U-Net with Attention for Diffusion:**

```python
import torch.nn as nn

class AttentionBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, channels):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.GroupNorm(32, channels)
        self.qkv = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels * 3, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 1)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        B, C, H, W = x.shape
        h = self.norm(x)
        qkv = self.qkv(h).reshape(B, 3, C, H*W)
        q, k, v = qkv.unbind(1)
        
        # Attention
        attn = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) / (C ** 0.5)
        attn = attn.softmax(-1)
        h = (attn @ v).reshape(B, C, H, W)
        
        return x + self.proj(h)

class DiffusionUNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels=3, model_channels=128):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Timestep embedding
        self.time_embed = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(model_channels, model_channels * 4),
            nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(model_channels * 4, model_channels * 4)
        )
        
        # Encoder
        self.down1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, model_channels, 3, padding=1)
        self.down2 = nn.Conv2d(model_channels, model_channels*2, 3, padding=1)
        self.attn = AttentionBlock(model_channels*2)
        
        # Bottleneck
        self.mid = nn.Conv2d(model_channels*2, model_channels*2, 3, padding=1)
        
        # Decoder
        self.up1 = nn.Conv2d(model_channels*4, model_channels, 3, padding=1)
        self.up2 = nn.Conv2d(model_channels*2, in_channels, 3, padding=1)
    
    def forward(self, x, t):
        # Get timestep embedding
        t_emb = self.get_timestep_embedding(t, 128)
        t_emb = self.time_embed(t_emb)
        
        # Encoder
        h1 = self.down1(x)
        h2 = self.down2(h1)
        h2 = self.attn(h2)
        
        # Bottleneck (add time embedding)
        h = self.mid(h2) + t_emb[..., None, None]
        
        # Decoder (with skip connections)
        h = self.up1(torch.cat([h, h2], 1))
        h = self.up2(torch.cat([h, h1], 1))
        
        return h
```
content.level4_expert:
**Classifier-Free Guidance Implementation:**

```python
class ConditionedDiffusion:
    def __init__(self, model, clip_model):
        self.model = model
        self.clip = clip_model
        self.null_embedding = torch.zeros(512)  # Unconditional
    
    @torch.no_grad()
    def sample_cfg(self, prompt, guidance_scale=7.5, steps=50):
        # Encode text
        text_emb = self.clip.encode_text(prompt)
        
        # DDIM sampling (faster than DDPM)
        x = torch.randn(1, 3, 512, 512)
        timesteps = torch.linspace(999, 0, steps).long()
        
        for t in timesteps:
            # Conditional prediction
            noise_cond = self.model(x, t, text_emb)
            
            # Unconditional prediction
            noise_uncond = self.model(x, t, self.null_embedding)
            
            # Classifier-free guidance
            noise = noise_uncond + guidance_scale * (noise_cond - noise_uncond)
            
            # DDIM update
            x = self.ddim_step(x, noise, t, timesteps)
        
        return x

# Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
class LatentDiffusion:
    def __init__(self, vae, unet, clip):
        self.vae = vae  # AutoencoderKL
        self.unet = unet
        self.clip = clip
    
    def generate(self, prompt, height=512, width=512):
        # Text embedding
        text_emb = self.clip.encode_text(prompt)
        
        # Latent space (8× smaller)
        latent_h, latent_w = height // 8, width // 8
        latent = torch.randn(1, 4, latent_h, latent_w)
        
        # Diffusion in latent space (much faster!)
        for t in reversed(range(50)):
            noise = self.unet(latent, t, text_emb)
            latent = self.denoise_step(latent, noise, t)
        
        # Decode to pixel space
        image = self.vae.decode(latent)
        return image
```

whatIsIt: Diffusion Models: Generative models via iterative denoising! Forward process: Clean image → gradually add Gaussian noise (1000 steps) → pure noise. Reverse process: Neural network learns to reverse. Start from noise → predict 'less noisy version' → iterate → clean image! Key: Markov chain (each step depends only on previous). Math: p(xₜ|xₜ₋₁) = N(√αₜ·xₜ₋₁, (1-αₜ)I). Training objective: Predict added noise ε. Architecture: U-Net with attention, timestep embedding, optional text conditioning (CLIP). Sampling: 50-1000 denoising steps. Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG): Amplify conditional vs unconditional prediction → better text alignment. Latent Diffusion: Work in VAE latent space (8× compression) → faster. State-of-the-art for image generation!
whyNeeded: Why Diffusion > GANs? (1) Training Stability: GANs notoriously unstable (mode collapse, discriminator-generator balance). Diffusion: Just denoise! Simple, stable objective. (2) Quality: Photorealistic images (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 2). (3) Mode Coverage: GANs miss modes (some image types). Diffusion: Better diversity. (4) Controllability: Text-to-image (conditioning), inpainting, editing. GANs harder to control. Applications: (1) Art Generation: Midjourney, Stable Diffusion XL. (2) Inpainting: Remove/add objects. (3) Super-resolution: Upscale images. (4) Image-to-image: Style transfer, editing. (5) Video generation: Extend to temporal dimension. Why slow? Iterative process (50-1000 steps vs GAN's 1 forward pass). Trade-off: Quality vs speed. Recent work: Faster samplers (DDIM, DPM-Solver). Latent diffusion: Speed up via smaller latent space. Revolutionary impact on generative AI!
realWorldAnalogy: Diffusion = Sculptor chipping marble! Start: Marble block (random noise). Process: Gradually remove unnecessary parts (denoise). Each chip (denoising step): Reveal more of final sculpture. Sculptor's skill (trained model): Knows what to remove at each stage. Text prompt: Blueprint! 'Make a cat statue' guides which parts to keep/remove. Why better than painter (GAN)? Painter: One stroke → might fail, hard to fix. Sculptor: Iterative refinement, always can adjust. Training: Watch sculptor work backwards! Sculpture → add clay randomly → blob. Learn reverse. Speed trade-off: Painting (GAN) = instant. Sculpting (Diffusion) = 50 careful steps, but better quality! Stable Diffusion = Sculpting miniature (latent space) then enlarging → faster!

stepByStep: 2. Sample random timestep t ~ Uniform(1, T)
algorithm.complexity: Training: O(T) per image (T timesteps). Sampling: O(T·model_forward). Model forward: U-Net O(H·W·C²). Typical: T=1000, H=W=64 (latent), 50-100 steps sampling. DDIM: Reduce steps to 50. Real-time: Not yet (vs GAN's instant).

import torch

def forward_diffusion(x0, t, alphas_cumprod):
    """Add noise to x0 at timestep t"""
    noise = torch.randn_like(x0)
    sqrt_alpha = torch.sqrt(alphas_cumprod[t])
    sqrt_one_minus = torch.sqrt(1 - alphas_cumprod[t])
    
    xt = sqrt_alpha * x0 + sqrt_one_minus * noise
    return xt, noise

# Example
x0 = torch.randn(1, 3, 64, 64)  # Clean image
betas = torch.linspace(0.0001, 0.02, 1000)
alphas_cumprod = torch.cumprod(1 - betas, 0)

xt, noise = forward_diffusion(x0, t=500, alphas_cumprod=alphas_cumprod)
print(f'Added noise at t=500: {xt.shape}')

codeExamples.title: Training Loop
codeExamples.code:
def train_diffusion(model, dataloader, timesteps=1000):
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-4)
    betas = torch.linspace(1e-4, 0.02, timesteps)
    alphas_cumprod = torch.cumprod(1 - betas, 0)
    
    for epoch in range(100):
        for x0 in dataloader:
            # Random timestep
            t = torch.randint(0, timesteps, (x0.shape[0],))
            
            # Add noise
            noise = torch.randn_like(x0)
            sqrt_alpha = torch.sqrt(alphas_cumprod[t])[:, None, None, None]
            sqrt_one_minus = torch.sqrt(1 - alphas_cumprod[t])[:, None, None, None]
            xt = sqrt_alpha * x0 + sqrt_one_minus * noise
            
            # Predict noise
            pred_noise = model(xt, t)
            
            # Loss
            loss = nn.MSELoss()(noise, pred_noise)
            
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
        
        print(f'Epoch {epoch}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}')

codeExamples.code:
@torch.no_grad()
def ddpm_sample(model, shape, timesteps=1000):
    betas = torch.linspace(1e-4, 0.02, timesteps)
    alphas = 1 - betas
    alphas_cumprod = torch.cumprod(alphas, 0)
    
    # Start from noise
    x = torch.randn(shape)
    
    for t in reversed(range(timesteps)):
        # Predict noise
        t_tensor = torch.full((shape[0],), t)
        pred_noise = model(x, t_tensor)
        
        # Coefficients
        alpha = alphas[t]
        alpha_cumprod = alphas_cumprod[t]
        beta = betas[t]
        
        # Denoise
        if t > 0:
            noise = torch.randn_like(x)
        else:
            noise = 0
        
        x = (1 / torch.sqrt(alpha)) * (
            x - ((1 - alpha) / torch.sqrt(1 - alpha_cumprod)) * pred_noise
        ) + torch.sqrt(beta) * noise
    
    return x

generated = ddpm_sample(model, (4, 3, 64, 64))

codeExamples.title: Classifier-Free Guidance
codeExamples.code:
@torch.no_grad()
def sample_with_cfg(model, text_embedding, guidance_scale=7.5, steps=50):
    """Generate with text conditioning"""
    null_emb = torch.zeros_like(text_embedding)  # Unconditional
    x = torch.randn(1, 4, 64, 64)  # Latent
    
    timesteps = torch.linspace(999, 0, steps).long()
    
    for t in timesteps:
        # Conditional
        noise_cond = model(x, t, text_embedding)
        
        # Unconditional
        noise_uncond = model(x, t, null_emb)
        
        # Guidance
        noise = noise_uncond + guidance_scale * (noise_cond - noise_uncond)
        
        # Denoise
        x = denoise_step(x, noise, t)
    
    return x

# Usage
text_emb = clip_model.encode('A cat wearing sunglasses')
image = sample_with_cfg(model, text_emb, guidance_scale=7.5)

codeExamples.title: DDIM Sampling (Faster)
codeExamples.code:
@torch.no_grad()
def ddim_sample(model, shape, steps=50):
    """DDIM: Deterministic, fewer steps"""
    x = torch.randn(shape)
    timesteps = torch.linspace(999, 0, steps).long()
    
    for i, t in enumerate(timesteps[:-1]):
        pred_noise = model(x, t)
        
        # Predict x0
        alpha_t = alphas_cumprod[t]
        x0_pred = (x - torch.sqrt(1 - alpha_t) * pred_noise) / torch.sqrt(alpha_t)
        
        # Next timestep
        t_next = timesteps[i + 1]
        alpha_next = alphas_cumprod[t_next]
        
        # DDIM update (deterministic!)
        x = torch.sqrt(alpha_next) * x0_pred + torch.sqrt(1 - alpha_next) * pred_noise
    
    return x

# 50 steps vs 1000! Much faster
generated = ddim_sample(model, (1, 3, 64, 64), steps=50)

quiz.question: Diffusion models'in temel prensibi nedir?
options: Iteratively denoise: Noise → gradually remove → image
quiz.explanation: Diffusion: Iterative denoising process! Forward: Image → add noise gradually → pure noise. Reverse (generation): Noise → trained model removes noise step by step → image. Unlike GANs (1 step generation) or VAE (encode-decode). Key: Learn to reverse noise addition process. Training: Predict added noise at random timesteps. Sampling: Start from random noise, denoise T times.

quiz.question: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) ne işe yarar?
options: Amplify conditional vs unconditional: Better text-image alignment
quiz.explanation: CFG: Guidance without classifier! Formula: ε̃ = ε_uncond + scale·(ε_cond - ε_uncond). Amplifies difference between conditional ('cat') and unconditional (empty) predictions. Effect: Stronger text alignment, more accurate to prompt. Scale 7-15 typical. Low (1-3): More creative, less accurate. High (15-20): Accurate but less diverse. Training: Randomly drop conditioning (50%) to learn both. Critical for text-to-image quality!

quiz.question: Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion) neden daha hızlı?
options: Work in compressed latent space (8× smaller): Much faster!
quiz.explanation: Latent Diffusion: Diffusion in VAE latent space! Instead of 512×512 pixels → 64×64 latent (8× compression). Benefits: (1) 64× fewer pixels to process → much faster! (2) Similar quality. (3) Lower memory. Process: Image → VAE encode → latent → diffusion → VAE decode → image. Stable Diffusion = Latent Diffusion + CLIP text conditioning. Breakthrough for practical text-to-image!

quiz.question: Diffusion vs GAN: En önemli avantaj?
options: Training stability & mode coverage: More reliable, diverse
quiz.explanation: Diffusion > GAN: (1) Training Stability: GANs notoriously unstable (mode collapse, balance issues). Diffusion: Simple denoising objective, stable! (2) Mode Coverage: GANs miss some image types. Diffusion: Better diversity. (3) Quality: State-of-the-art (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 2). Disadvantage: Speed (50-1000 steps vs GAN's 1). Trade-off: Quality & stability vs speed. Use case: When quality matters more than speed!

quiz.question: DDIM vs DDPM sampling farkı nedir?
options: DDIM: Deterministic, fewer steps (50 vs 1000), faster!
quiz.explanation: DDPM: Original sampling. Stochastic (random noise each step), needs ~1000 steps. DDIM: Deterministic sampling! Same noise → same image. Fewer steps (50) with similar quality. How: Directly predict x₀, then jump to next timestep (skip intermediate). Benefits: 20× faster, consistent outputs, can invert images. Use: Default in Stable Diffusion. DDPM: When you need stochasticity/exploration.

quiz.question: Text-to-image diffusion'da text nasıl kullanılır?
options: CLIP text embedding → Cross-attention in U-Net: Conditions each denoising step
quiz.explanation: Text Conditioning: (1) Encode text via CLIP → embedding vector. (2) U-Net has cross-attention layers: Image features attend to text embedding. (3) Each denoising step conditioned on text. (4) CFG amplifies text influence. Process: Text guides what to denoise into! 'Cat' → model removes noise to reveal cat features. Without text: Random generation. With text: Controlled generation. CLIP: Trained to align text-image → perfect for conditioning!

commonMistakes.why: 10-20 steps → blurry, low quality images. Model needs time to progressively refine! Each step adds details.
commonMistakes.fix: Use 50+ steps for quality. DDIM: 50 steps good balance. DDPM: 1000 steps. Trade-off: Quality vs speed. For fast preview: 25 steps OK. For final: 50-100 steps. Don't go below 20!

commonMistakes.why: Scale = 1 → ignores text prompt! Scale = 30 → oversaturated, artifacts. Too much guidance = instability.
commonMistakes.fix: Optimal CFG scale: 7-7.5 for most prompts. Artistic: 5-7. Photorealistic: 7-9. Highly detailed: 9-12. Never >20. Experiment per use case. Scale affects: Text alignment (higher → more accurate), diversity (lower → more variety), artifacts (too high → issues).

commonMistakes.mistake: Not using latent diffusion for large images
commonMistakes.why: Diffusion on 512×512 pixels → very slow! High memory. Impractical for real-time.
commonMistakes.fix: Use Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)! Diffusion in 64×64 latent space → 8× compression → 64× speed improvement. Same quality. Essential for practical applications. Pixel-space diffusion: Only for small images (<128×128) or research.

commonMistakes.why: Linear β schedule [1e-4, 0.02] → suboptimal for some data. Too much/little noise at timesteps.
commonMistakes.fix: Tune variance schedule! Linear: Good start. Cosine: Often better (stable late timesteps). Quadratic: Some cases. Monitor: Noise levels at different t. Too noisy early → increase β. Not noisy enough late → decrease. Critical for training stability and quality!

commonMistakes.why: Model doesn't know which timestep → can't denoise appropriately! Different denoising needed at t=100 vs t=900.
commonMistakes.fix: Always include timestep embedding! Sinusoidal encoding (like Transformer). Inject into model (usually after attention). Formula: embed(t) = [sin(ωₖ·t), cos(ωₖ·t)] for k frequencies. Crucial: Model must know noise level to denoise correctly!

commonMistakes.why: Training only conditional → can't do CFG! Need unconditional ε_∅ for formula: ε̃ = ε_∅ + scale·(ε_c - ε_∅).
commonMistakes.fix: Train with random conditioning dropout! 10-20% of time: Replace text embedding with null/empty. Model learns both: Conditional (with text) and unconditional (without). During inference: Can do CFG. Essential for text-to-image quality!

commonMistakes.why: Too aggressive schedule → training unstable. Too gentle → slow convergence. Affects generation quality!
commonMistakes.fix: Start with proven schedules: Linear [1e-4, 0.02] (good default), Cosine (better for high-res), Sigmoid (some cases). Monitor: Loss curve, generated quality. Adjust: If unstable → reduce max β. If slow → increase. Don't create from scratch without reason!

visualizations.title: Forward & Reverse Diffusion Process
visualizations.description: Animation: Clean image → gradually add noise (1000 steps) → pure noise. Then reverse: Noise → iteratively denoise → clean image. Side-by-side visualization.

visualizations.title: DDPM vs DDIM vs GAN Speed-Quality
visualizations.description: Chart: X=Speed, Y=Quality. DDPM (slow, high quality), DDIM (medium, high quality), GAN (fast, good quality). Latent Diffusion: Sweet spot!

visualizations.title: CFG Scale Effect
visualizations.description: Slider: CFG scale 1-20. Shows same prompt with different scales. Low: Creative, diverse. High: Accurate, less variety. Artifacts at extremes.

visualizations.title: Stable Diffusion Architecture
visualizations.description: Diagram: Text → CLIP → Embedding. Image → VAE → Latent. U-Net(latent, timestep, text) → Denoised. VAE decoder → Final image. Full pipeline!

references.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
